name: Blue Mountain
generated_description:
At 1,949 feet, Blue Mountain is a summit in Alabama. The Blue Mountain Trail covers 0.9 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 250 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

Most of the climbing comes early — the first half of the route does the bulk of the work before the grade eases. Along the way the route passes a viewpoint (Bald Rock Overlook) near mile 0, a hut (Blue Mountain Shelter) near mile 0.44 — useful checkpoints for judging your pace.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 33.4955, -85.8077 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 85 miles west of Atlanta, Georgia. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

This trail is hikeable most of the year. Summer brings heat and humidity — carry extra water — while fall and spring offer the most comfortable conditions. Ice is possible on shaded stretches in mid-winter.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Cheaha Mountain, McDill Point and Little Caney Head — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.question: When is the best time to hike Blue Mountain?
faqs.answer: Most of the year. Fall and spring are most comfortable; summer is hot and humid, and ice is possible on shaded stretches in mid-winter.

faqs.question: How tall is Blue Mountain?
faqs.answer: Blue Mountain stands at 1,949 feet (594 meters) in Alabama.
